entities.name: Cadwgan ap Bleddyn
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Cadwgan ap Bleddyn (1051–1111) was the second son of Bleddyn ap Cynfyn, King of Powys and Gwynedd.

    As the prince of the Kingdom of Powys in north eastern Wales, Cadwgan played a significant role in the medieval politics of the region.

    His reign was marked by a series of struggles against the neighboring Kingdom of Gwynedd, led by his cousin, Gruffydd ap Cynan.

    In 1094, Cadwgan was crowned King of Powys, but his reign was short-lived as he died in 1111.

    Cadwgan's legacy is largely overshadowed by his cousin Gruffydd ap Cynan, who went on to become a powerful and influential king in his own right.

    Despite this, Cadwgan's contributions to the history of Wales and the medieval period are significant, and his story serves as a reminder of the complex and often tumultuous nature of medieval politics.
